name: Maje
band_note: mean of blouse and sweater entry $255 (women's price pass, 2026-10-13)
why: Parisian women's dresses, knitwear, tailoring, leather jackets and bags, with dresses around $300–550, sold through its own stores, site and department stores.
origin: Founded in Paris, France in 1998 by Judith Milgrom.

quote.q: Twenty years ago, I created Maje for women like me. Women who constantly change.

opview: “Twenty years ago, I created Maje for women like me. Women who constantly change.” — Judith Milgrom, founder, Judith Milgrom page, maje.com

doors.note: site us.maje.com (/en/stores redirects to /en/boutiques); 56 US rows: 16 boutiques, 6 outlets (typed 'outlet' by the locator) and 34 department-store listings (31 Bloomingdale's, 3 Saks) under the locator's 'Department stores' type; the locator gives no sign of a branded shop, so ruled 10 Oct: counters, kept in return_doors.csv with the store group as operator and counted nowhere; the locator's own US filter (?country=US) reads '55 stores within 3,000 miles', the 56th being Bloomingdale's Ala Moana in Honolulu; Bloomie's Mosaic store page is empty, address from the card; 1 ZIP+4 cut; no US pop-ups or coming-soon; plus 34 department-store counter row(s), kept in return_doors.csv and counted nowhere

fibre.sample: stratified sample of 80 from 589 women's clothing styles (reference stem, e.g. MFPPU01061, before the colour code) on /en/categories/view-all-clothing/?sz=800;

craft_evidence.owned: no — 'a network of factories and workshops located in different countries' (auditing-suppliers page)
craft_evidence.madein: 0% in page text — country of manufacture is delivered through a Fairly Made traceability widget and label QR codes, not
craft_evidence.heritage: none found in the about-maje page text read
craft_evidence.process: partial — traceability programme with Fairly Made maps production stages; no making process described
craft_evidence.reasoning: Maje says it makes through a network of third-party factories and owns none. A Fairly Made traceability programme publishes the country of manufacture per product through a widget or QR code, so there is a checkable country trail but no maker or mill. Sourcing transparency earns a 2.
